# Proposal: Fractional AI Governance Advisor

**Prepared for:** Dana Whitfield, General Counsel, Tamarack Instruments
**Program:** Fractional AI Governance Advisor, AI Governance Academy
**Basis:** Client Profile Block v1.0 and discovery call notes of 6 October 2026 (participants: Dana Whitfield, Ravi Okafor and Ingrid Solberg)

## 1. Situation Summary

Tamarack Instruments designs and manufactures laboratory measurement instruments. It has about 1,100 staff and operates in the Netherlands, Germany and the United States, with headquarters in the Netherlands. The Client has not completed a prior Academy program, so this proposal starts from the Client's current position.

The Client's AI portfolio is at the piloting stage of maturity. It includes:

* A customer service chatbot deployed on the support portal.
* An AI visual inspection pilot on the German production line.
* AI sales forecasting, planned for next year.

The regulatory drivers named are the EU AI Act and GDPR. The certification target is ISO/IEC 42001. That work is set to start next year, but the start date is not fixed.

An internal audit finding in June 2026 recorded that there is no inventory of AI systems.

The Client names ISO/IEC 27001 (ISMS) and ISO 9001 (quality management system) as incumbent frameworks. This proposal does not assume that any particular register, process or control already exists under them. Whether existing management system processes can be extended to AI is Unknown and will be assessed in Quarter 1.

Your stated objective is direct: "I want governance in place before visual inspection goes into production in Q2 2027." Three constraints shape how that objective can be met:

* Customer data must stay in the EU.
* The German works council must be consulted before anything touches production staff.
* Budget is approved up to US$80,000 this fiscal year.

## 2. The Case for Continuous Fractional Advisory at the Piloting Stage

At the piloting stage, governance decisions are made alongside delivery decisions rather than after them. The visual inspection pilot is moving toward production, the chatbot is already live and a third use case is planned. A one-time assessment would describe the position at a single point. A fractional advisor stays with the Client as each system moves from pilot to production and as ISO/IEC 42001 work begins.

Three areas need sustained attention rather than a single intervention:

* **The AI inventory gap.** The internal audit finding is foundational. Every later governance artifact depends on knowing which AI systems exist.
* **The production timeline.** Governance for visual inspection needs to be ready before Q2 2027. That includes preparing for works council consultation, the timing of which is not yet known.
* **Readiness for certification.** ISO/IEC 42001 preparation is more efficient when the evidence is designed in from the start rather than reconstructed later.

The engagement applies two open frameworks, which remain available to the Client after the engagement ends:

* GRC Workbook (https://github.com/rolldabones/grc-workbook)
* Slow AI Kitchen (https://github.com/rolldabones/slow-ai-kitchen)

Executive and board-level material draws on AI Governance for Boards (https://github.com/rolldabones/ai-governance-for-boards).

The engagement is guided by three principles: Slow AI, Informed Intent, Final Liability rests with the Human.

## 3. The Annual Arc

The engagement runs in four quarters. The engagement start date is Unknown and is flagged for intake. If the engagement begins in January 2027, engagement Quarter 2 falls in calendar Q2 2027, when visual inspection is planned to go into production. A later start would compress Quarter 1, so the start date bears directly on the stated objective.

**Quarter 1: Stabilize.** Establish the governance foundation that the production timeline depends on:

* Build the AI system inventory in response to the June 2026 audit finding.
* Define governance roles and an intake path for new AI use cases.
* Assess whether the ISO/IEC 27001 and ISO 9001 management system processes can host AI governance.
* Begin the governance file for visual inspection, covering risk assessment, human oversight design and documentation.
* Prepare governance inputs for the works council consultation. Who leads the consultation is Unknown.
* Prepare questions for external counsel on how the EU AI Act classifies the visual inspection and chatbot use cases. These are flagged for counsel verification and are not resolved by the advisor.

**Quarter 2: Deepen.** Support the visual inspection production decision:

* Run a governance readiness review before go-live, including post-deployment monitoring and escalation arrangements.
* Review the deployed chatbot against the requirement that customer data stays in the EU. The chatbot's current data handling is Unknown and will be established during this review.
* Mature the inventory and intake process for ongoing use.

**Quarter 3: Assure.** Turn to ISO/IEC 42001 readiness:

* Map current governance artifacts to the standard's requirements and identify gaps.
* Organize evidence collection.
* Prepare for internal audit review of AI governance.

The intensity of audit preparation in this quarter depends on the ISO/IEC 42001 start date and any external audit date. Both are Unknown and flagged for intake, and the quarter will be resequenced once they are known.

**Quarter 4: Evolve.**

* Take the planned AI sales forecasting use case through the intake process.
* Review regulatory developments flagged during the year, for verification by counsel.
* Consolidate the ISO/IEC 42001 readiness position.
* Prepare renewal or handover options.

All audit preparation is described in readiness terms. The engagement does not promise any certification or audit outcome.

## 4. Cadence and Access Model

* **Monthly executive advisory session:** decisions, risks and direction.
* **Monthly working session with the governance team:** artifact development and implementation guidance.
* **Asynchronous availability:** for defined question categories, with response windows set in the cadence kit.
* **Quarterly governance review:** progress against the annual plan and readiness status.

The Profile Block names these audience roles: General Counsel, CISO, Head of Quality, Head of Data, German plant manager and two internal auditors. Attendance at each session is Unknown and will be confirmed at intake.

## 5. Scope

**In scope:** governance evolution, implementation guidance, audit preparation, AI strategy and executive decision support.

**Out of scope:** legal advice, certification body functions, staff augmentation and incident command.

The advisor is not counsel of record. Legal questions, including EU AI Act classification and GDPR interpretation, are routed to external counsel. Regulatory developments the advisor raises are flagged for verification and are never presented as settled advice.

## 6. Investment

The engagement is priced at US$10,000 per month for 12 months and is renewable.

The approved budget of up to US$80,000 this fiscal year covers eight months at US$10,000 per month. The fiscal year end date is Unknown. As a result, both of the following are flagged for resolution before a decision:

* How many engagement months fall within the current fiscal year.
* How the remaining months will be funded in the following fiscal year.
